Curriculum vitae

David P. McGinnis, Ph.D.

Accelerator physicist and electrical engineer with experience in accelerator operations, radio-frequency systems, instrumentation and control.

← About BL Monitor and Control View publications on INSPIRE

Professional experience

BL Monitor and Control AB

Co-founder and CTO · Lund, Sweden · 2021–present

Developing Blinky-Lite and integrating monitoring and control solutions for research and industry.

MAX IV Laboratory

Accelerator Division · Lund, Sweden · 2018–2025

Research Engineer in the RF Group and RF Group Leader.

European Spallation Source

Accelerator Division · Lund, Sweden · 2011–2018

Senior Accelerator Advisor, Chief Engineer and Radio Frequency Group Leader.

Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory

Accelerator science and engineering · Batavia, Illinois, USA · 1988–2011

Held scientific, engineering and leadership roles across the accelerator complex, including Associate Accelerator Division Head for Systems, Integration and Operations; Run II Upgrades Technical Manager; and department head positions in the Antiproton Source, Proton Source and Booster Synchrotron.

Other work included Project X concept development, accelerator software, radio-frequency and microwave engineering, and instrumentation for the 21 cm project.

University of Wisconsin–Madison

Postdoctoral Research Associate · Madison, Wisconsin, USA · 1987–1988

Research in superconducting radio-frequency devices.

Selected accomplishments

ESS accelerator design

As Chief Engineer of the ESS Accelerator Division, led a 2012–2014 linac redesign that reduced the estimated cost by €75 million and became the new accelerator baseline.

Explore the ESS linac design

American Physical Society Fellow

Elected in 2003 for contributions to increasing the performance of the Fermilab accelerator complex.

Fermilab accelerator operations

As Associate Accelerator Division Head, oversaw systems, integration and operations across the accelerator complex, including a period of substantially increased Tevatron luminosity.

RF, microwave and beam systems

Led and contributed to stochastic cooling upgrades, beam-stabilization systems and accelerator instrumentation, including work on the Fermilab Antiproton Source.

Teaching and mentoring

David has taught radio-frequency and microwave topics as a Visiting Professor at the University of Chicago, an Adjunct Professor at Northern Illinois University and the Illinois Institute of Technology, and an instructor for the United States Particle Accelerator School.

He has also advised two graduate students in the Fermilab Accelerator Physics Program.

  • Radio Frequency and Microwave Physics Concepts and Techniques
  • Microwave Measurements and Beam Instrumentation Laboratory
